page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with marginal notes on the right. Running head at top, page number at top right. Footnote marks 1, 2 and 3 stand in the right margin beside the text. Catchword at lower right, gathering signature at lower left. The strip at the left edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.l: tis præmia decernuntur, vel legum violatoribus
constituta sunt supplicia, vel indiscriminatim u-
triflibet in judiciis jura dicuntur? quorum sunt
illi, Legum actus primi, & per modum Formæ:
isti remotiores, & per modum Effectus. Annon eo
demum fine, ut Respublica in pace & tranquillitate
floreat; & ut privati etiam cives publicæ felicitatis
participipio, pro suo cujusque modulo & mensur-
a, gaudeant & fruantur? hoc est uno verbo, ut com-
muni utilitati inserviatur. Probatur denique tertio,
à Posteriori, ex omnium hominum sensu consen-
suque. Nam & qui justa decernunt Legumlatores,
revera videntur; & qui meditantur malum sicut
Legem, videri tamen cupiunt, in ferendis legibus
non tàm suam, quàm communem utilitatem respe-
xisse. Εἴτε σαφρονῶν[?], εἴτε ἀληθείας[?], five id sincerè
intendant, five subdole obtendant, qui Leges aliis
dicunt; propositum fuisse sibi in ferendis Legibus
Bonum Publicum, profitentur utcunque uni-
versi.
II. Hoc ita jacto disputationis fundamento, Le-
gum finem esse Bonum Communitatis; ad Dubia
pergo. Quorum esto primum, an sit Legum Hu-
manarum usus aliquis, saltem necessarius? Cui
nullus foret in hac (Dubiorum dico) classe conce-
dendus locus, nisi hoc nobis facesseret negotium
Anabaptistarum, aliorumque cum ipsis juxta sen-
tentiam, vesanus error. Ex quorum principiis,
(quum negent licere viro Christiano Magistratum
gerere, bello liteve contendere, jurare aut alteri
juramentum deferre aliaque consimilia :) conse-
qui videtur, omninò nullam esse Legum Humana-
rum necessitatem. Nec enim erit, sublatâ Jurisdic-
tione, qui Leges ferat: nec sublatis Judiciis, qui
reformidet. Quid testes quærimonia, si non
supplicio culpa reciditur? Quid vana sine moribus

page.notes: Left edge strip is the neighbouring page, not transcribed. The Greek phrase after "meditantur malum sicut Legem" is hard to read and is uncertain throughout. The first footnote reads "Prov. ?." with a number that is unclear; read as 8 with 15 below it. Footnote 2 "Psal. 94." and "10." are both read from the right margin. The note "Horat. 3." is in the right margin, with "Ode 24." on the line below. The right margin number "3." beside "tertio" is a section numeral, given as a note. Printed letter forms such as "liteve" and "vana sine" are uncertain; "Quid vana sine moribus" continues past the end of the scan. Long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as plain s.
